newsitem.title: MEXICO: Calm elections catapult Mexico shrs to new record.
newsitem.headline: Calm elections catapult Mexico shrs to new record.

text.p: The Mexican stock exchange soared to its fifth record close in a row Monday, following Sunday's midterm elections, which have been relatively free of the fraud allegations that marred past elections, dealers said.
"The most important event of the year is now behind us with no major casualties," said Gordon Lee, a stock analyst with Deutsche Morgan Grenfell-Mexico.
The blue-chip IPC index closed up 96.70 points on the day, or 2.08 percent, at a new record of 4,741.30.
"The fact the parties recognised each others' victories, and the speed and extent of that recognition was a very mature response," Lee added. "There was something for everybody in this election."
Mexicans voted Sunday and a preliminary count showed Cuauhtemoc Cardenas, of the left-wing Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD) with a 22-point lead in the historic Mexico City race.
President Ernesto Zedillo, of the ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI), congratulated Cardenas on Sunday night.
Early returns also showed the conservative National Action Party (PAN) had wrested control of two states from the PRI.
The PRI, meanwhile, was heading to lose its overall majority in the lower house, but was still the largest single party and may have retained at least two states.

"The bourse is still climbing as it has lagged behind other Latam markets. Now it has decoupled from the elections, we also have lower interest rates in the offing," said Lars Schonander, research head at Santander Investment-Mexico.
Lee added that post-electoral calm helped the market shrug off a slide of 37.32 points on the Dow Jones Industrial Average, which closed at 7,858.49.
Dealers said blue chips drove the market, notably from the financial sector.
"As there were relatively few post-electoral problems, the outlook for domestic interest rates is downward," said Enrique Pani, a banking analyst at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell-Mexico.

Bancomer, one of Mexico's biggest financial groups, gained 40 centavos (5 cents) to 4.42 pesos (56 cents). The group's A and B shares together accounted for almost one-quarter of all shares traded, dealers said, on heavy foreign demand.

Telefonos de Mexico (Telmex) leaped 70 centavos (9 cents) to a record close in peso terms of 20.60 pesos ($2.60). The telecom firm's ADRs meanwhile climbed 2-1/8 to 51-7/8, their highest level since the December 1994 peso crisis.
Dealers also drew attention to gains by construction company firm Empresas ICA and cement maker Cemex, both of which are market heavyweights.
ICA gained 5.70 pesos (72 cents) to 141.50 pesos ($17.85), while Cemex was up 55 centavos (7 cents) to 36.50 pesos ($4.61).
Trading volume was heavy at 142.6 million shares. The broad market mirrored buoyant blue chips, with gainers outnumbering sliders by 81 to 22, out of a total of 127 stocks that changed hands.
